originality.rationale: PASS: The motivating 2026 primary text has its Section 4.1 fold and its Theorem 4 strict inequalities but not the equality-case global extinction law or coefficients. Its Theorem 8 cusp is at a positive coexistence equilibrium with the cusp carrying capacity equal to twice the response optimum, whereas this is predator-free at the carrying capacity equal to the response optimum. Theorem 7 requires a positive coexistence equilibrium absent under our parameters. The 2025 nearest Holling-IV additional-food paper has an explicit negative quadratic predator crowding term, which changes the leading predator drift and does not imply the uncrowded half-power law. Indexed semantic searches found only other critical-rate or predator-prey models; current and earlier own-claim ledgers contained no matching source/threshold. General cubic center dynamics explains an exponent but not the exact global all-positive-data assertion. An inaccessible 2019 related source remains a bounded literature risk, not an observed covering result.

value.rationale: PASS: The two natural ecological equality conditions—mortality exactly equals the greatest possible numerical response and carrying capacity equals the prey density of that maximum—meet at a predator-free boundary collision. Standard linear extinction tests become inconclusive. The result determines whether predators persist globally and quantifies the critical persistence time and prey shortfall by sharp initial-data-independent constants. Its cubic effective drift, and consequent half-power decay rather than exponential decay or the inverse-time competition-dominated case, is a structural biological distinction, not a parametric numerical exercise.
